doc.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Tony Williams in Pacifica and his death
summary: Tony lived nearby, and Bobby believes a misdiagnosis at Seton Hospital after a gall bladder operation cost him his life.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Really? Because I knew he had a place in San Anselmo. I didn’t know he was living down in Pacifica.

Yeah, he moved down here. I used to see Tony at the bank. Tony – I’d be standing in line at the bank, and Tony would come up and hit my leg and make my legs bend, pow. Hey. Tony was something. His mom – he had a beautiful mother. His mother looked like his sister. She looked so young. She stayed here when Tony died. She stayed here at our house. Tony wasn’t supposed to die. They – wrong diagnosis at the hospital.
He had originally gone in for a gall bladder operation?
Yeah, it was – they completely missed the diagnosis. Tony should still be with us.
Do you know anything more about that? What . . . ?

Yeah, they just did the wrong thing, and then everybody passed the buck at the hospital, Seton Hospital, right over here. They just passed the buck on it. Yeah, Tony should still be with us. He told his wife – he says – after they have the operation, he says, “I still feel something’s wrong.” They completely missed everything. Sometimes some of these doctors, they’re like McDonald’s or something. They just – “Okay. Who’s next?” You know what I mean? “Okay. How much time do I have to perform this operation.”
The families, did they – any kind of lawsuit or any malpractice?
No. Not that I know of. They know how to pass the buck.
